sentences.text: The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar

Writ Petition No.15285 of 2023
Order:

This Writ Petition is filed seeking to grant the following relief:
"... to issue a writ or order more particularly one in the nature of the WRIT OF MANDAMUS declaring the action of the respondents in not renewing the petitioner's passport bearing No.J6327268 in turn issued show cause notice vide Letter No.SCN/312386977/22 dt.29.03.2022 to the petitioner, as illegal, arbitrary, unjust,
unconstitutional and in violation of Articles 14, 19 and 21 of Indian Constitution and against the principles of natural justice and

consequently set aside the show cause notice, dated 29.03.2022 vide Letter Ref No.SCN/312386977/22 issued by respondent No.2 by directing them to renew the petitioner's passport bearing No.J6327268 and hand over the same to the petitioner and to pass such other order or orders as this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper in the interest of justice."
2. Heard Sri K.L.B. Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Gadi Praveen Kumar, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India, appearing for the respondents.
3.
It is the case of the petitioner that he was holding a passport bearing No.J6327268 valid from 25.07.2011 till 24.07.2021, issued by respondent No.2.
Since the validity of the passport expired, the petitioner made an online application bearing No.BN1073982544722, dated 24.02.2022, before respondent No.2 seeking reissue/renewal of the passport.

The respondents, while taking steps for renewal of the passport of the petitioner, came to know about the pendency of a criminal case in C.C.No.6350 of 2021 pending on the file of II Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad,
for the offences under Section 506 and 509 of I.P.C.

entities.text: II Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In view of pendency of the said criminal case,
respondent No.2 kept the application of the petitioner pending for renewal of the same.
Aggrieved by such action of respondent No.2, the petitioner approached this Court by filing the present writ petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner also placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Vangala Kasturi Rangacharuyulu v. Central Bureau of Investigation1, wherein the provisions of the Passports Act, 1967 (for short, 'the Act, 1967') were examined, pending criminal cases against the applicants, and held that a passport can be refused only in case where the applicant is convicted during the period of five years immediately preceding the date of application for an offence involving moral turpitude and sentence for imprisonment for not less than two years.

entities.text: Vangala Kasturi Rangacharuyulu v. Central Bureau of Investigation1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Section 6 (2)
(f) of the Act, 1967 relates to a situation where the applicant is facing trial in a criminal Court.

The petitioner therein was convicted in a case for the offences under Sections 420,
468, 471 and 477A read with 120B of the I.P.C., and also Section 13 (2) read with 13 (1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Against which, an appeal was filed and the same was dismissed.

sentences.text: The sentence was reduced to a period of one year.
The petitioner therein had approached the Hon'ble Apex Court by way of filing an appeal and the same is pending.
Therefore, considering the said facts, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the Passport Authority cannot refuse renewal of the passport on the ground of pendency of the criminal appeal.
Thus, the Hon'ble Apex Court directed the Passport Authority to renew the passport of the applicant without raising the objection relating to the pendency of the aforesaid criminal appeal.

5. Sri Gadi Praveen Kumar, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India, appearing for the respondents, submitted that the renewal of the passport cannot be granted to the applicant, in case,
if any criminal case is pending against the said applicant.

He further submitted that said issue is dealt with by the learned Single Judge of this Court in the case of Pervez Mohammad Abdul v. Union of India and another2 and the issue of renewal of the passport be governed by the very same judgment.

entities.text: Pervez Mohammad Abdul v. Union of India and another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the petitioner, contended that renewal of the passport is different from issuance of fresh passport.

7. This Court, having considered the submissions made on either side and after perusing the material on record including the judgments in the cases of Vangala Kasturi Rangacharuyulu and Pervez Mohammad Abdul (1 and 2 supra), is of the considered view that in the light of Section 6 of the Act, 1967, the renewal/re-issue of passport is also governed by the very same provisions and restrictions as are applicable for issuing a fresh or renewal of the passport.
Admittedly, a criminal case is pending against the petitioner herein before the competent Court.

Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that the application of the petitioner can be directed to be considered by imposing restrictions and conditions as were imposed in the case of Pervez Mohammad Abdul.

sentences.text: vi) However, liberty is granted to the petitioner herein to file a petition before the trial Court in the aforesaid calendar case seeking permission to travel abroad.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall also stand closed.
